en.title: The office enters an economy of verifiable capacity
keypoints: Market recovery opens a window to reposition, but does not save assets lacking defensible cost, experience and data.
Hybrid work and AI require value to be measured by in-person activity and portfolios to retain contractual flexibility.
Grid capacity and ESG traceability now shape timetable, CAPEX and asset value.
en.body:
01 Executive summary

The office is entering an economy of verifiable capacity. The market is improving, yet space, a hybrid policy, an ESG plan or AI tools are no longer enough; each promise must become measurable operating performance.

The tension sits between ten-year real-estate decisions and technology, energy and regulatory cycles measured in months. The competitive asset will coordinate people, flex costs, manage power and demonstrate results without losing human quality.

02 Signals of the week

Recent news and data through the lens of the sustainable, profitable workplace.

Market recovery buys time, not immunity for an asset

CBRE Research · 29 July 2026

US office vacancy fell 30 basis points in the second quarter to 18.3%, its largest quarterly fall of the cycle. CBRE expects annual leasing to exceed 2022 levels.

Aggregate improvement eases pressure but does not solve operating cost, experience or obsolescence. An improving market can conceal assets without a defensible proposition.

▸ Work&Place reading: Profitable sustainability becomes a defence of liquidity. Energy, flexibility, environmental quality and operating data determine which asset captures the recovery.

▸ Second order / owner and Real Estate: If improvement persists for 3–6 months, dispersion will widen between buildings that sustain rent and those that participate only through incentives or deferred CAPEX.

Hybrid work is no longer a transition: its bill appears in coordination

Gallup / Fortune–Robin · 27 July 2026

Gallup puts 52% of remote-capable US employees in hybrid work, averaging 2.3 office days a week and barely changed since 2023. Robin estimates hybrid logistics consume 10% of the working week and cost $14,000 per employee annually — an estimate from a vendor, but one that points to a cost rarely included in the business case.

Gallup supplies the contrast: teams with a formal collaboration plan are 66% more likely to be engaged and 29% less likely to experience burnout. Presence creates value only when a system of work exists.

▸ Work&Place reading: The office-club needs choreography: activities, spaces, technology and shared norms. Occupancy without purpose transfers friction to calendars, meeting rooms and talent.

▸ Second order / CHRO and CFO: If the pattern persists, the hidden cost of hybrid work will enter productivity and retention. Teams that measure outcomes by activity, rather than attendance days, will win.

AI shortens the real-estate horizon before it optimises the building

Facilities Dive / IWG–JLL · 28 July 2026; Contracting Business / Carrier · 28 July 2026

Sixty percent of 1,000 CEOs and CFOs surveyed by IWG say AI makes their two-year space need harder to forecast; 73% avoid long property commitments. Operational maturity trails that concern: only 15% of 2,200 global leaders surveyed by JLL have moved from initial AI deployment to optimisation in Real Estate.

Carrier’s acquisition of 75F brings sensors, controls, analytics, auto-commissioning and agentic AI together. Capital is demanding flexibility as technology starts to affect maintenance, energy and comfort.

▸ Work&Place reading: Useful AI connects a use case, reliable data, a decision and an accountable owner. Buying capability without governance increases dependency and reduces comparability.

▸ Second order / CFO, FM and operator: Flexible leases and integrated platforms will grow, along with lock-in, data risk and the need for common scenarios across IT, FM and Finance.

Grid connection shifts from technical formality to viability condition

NL Times / NOS–Stedin · 26 July 2026; Schneider Electric Research Institute · 28 July 2026

De Nieuwe Tuin, a former Rabobank building vacant for more than ten years, secured priority grid connection in Utrecht by installing two generators to relieve peak congestion. Without the agreement, the redevelopment would have waited years.

Schneider modelled 65 EV-charging cases: smart management kept every one within the grid limit. In a large office it can avoid more than €100,000 of CAPEX and a second 2,000 kVA transformer.

▸ Work&Place reading: The sustainable office becomes an active energy asset. Contracted capacity, charging flexibility and peak control belong in due diligence and design from the outset.

▸ Second order / owner, FM and operator: If congestion persists, power access will determine timetable, rent and value. BMS, charging and storage will compete as tools for avoided CAPEX.

CSRD narrows the perimeter while making data less comparable

EFRAG / ESG Today · 27 July 2026

EFRAG’s draft ESRS for large non-EU groups would reduce the scope from about 10,000 companies to 1,200. It focuses on impacts and drops risks, opportunities, resilience and dependencies; combining global and EU-limited information may weaken comparability.

Fewer entities required to report does not reduce the need for operating data. Energy, water, air, waste, occupancy and suppliers must remain traceable at building level.

▸ Work&Place reading: The building remains a unit of evidence, even when the legal reporting perimeter narrows.

▸ Second order / CFO and Real Estate: Banks, clients and investors may demand their own bridges of comparability, shifting cost from standard reporting to bilateral questionnaires.

03 Indicators to watch

  • US office vacancy 18.3% · CBRE Q2 2026; down 30 basis points quarter-on-quarter.
  • Hybrid work among remote-capable employees 52% · Gallup Q2 2026; 2.3 office days weekly.
  • Estimated hybrid-work friction 10% of the week · Robin via Fortune; $14,000 per employee annually.
  • Teams with a formal collaboration plan +66% engagement · Gallup; 29% lower likelihood of burnout.
  • Real Estate leaders optimising AI 15% · JLL, 2,200 leaders across 21 countries.
  • CEOs/CFOs avoiding long leases because of technological change 73% · IWG/Censuswide.
  • Cases staying within grid limit using smart charging 65 out of 65 · Schneider Electric.
  • Non-EU companies estimated to remain in CSRD scope 1,200 · EFRAG.

04 What roadmap should I set?

One concrete action for each role. Six-minute read; one decision out.

ProfilePriority action
OwnerTest every asset against grid connection, peak-control CAPEX, defensible rent and retrofit timetable. Flag dependencies that could delay occupation.
Tenant / CHROCreate a team agreement for one critical in-person activity: who meets, which space they use, the result it produces and friction over four weeks.
Facility ManagerMeasure peak power, EV charging, energy per used workstation and room incidents for seven days. Identify one shiftable load and quantify savings.
Operator / Real EstateBuild three 24-month portfolio scenarios — base, accelerated AI and contraction — with area, contractual flexibility, cost per useful workstation and exit route.
CFORequire a baseline, data owner, expected saving, integration cost and portability clause from every real-estate AI initiative.
CEOPut one question to the committee for each site: which business capability does it protect? Link the answer to a customer, talent, innovation or continuity metric.

es.title: La recuperación de la oficina se convierte en una criba operativa
keypoints: La mejora de la demanda separa activos defendibles de oficinas cuyo mejor caso económico es cambiar de uso.
El híbrido estable obliga a medir valor presencial por actividad, no asistencia bruta.
BMS, CSRD e IA convierten la calidad del dato y la resiliencia operativa en variables financieras.
es.body:
01 Resumen ejecutivo

La tesis de la semana: la recuperación de la oficina se ha convertido en un mecanismo de selección. La demanda mejora, pero el capital, el talento y la regulación distinguen con más dureza entre activos operables y metros cuadrados prescindibles.

El patrón común es la evidencia. Ocupación útil, dato ESG, ciberseguridad y consumo de recursos ya deciden renta, CAPEX y productividad. La oficina sostenible gana cuando permite decidir mejor; la que no demuestra función, rendimiento y resiliencia entra en descuento o conversión.

02 Señales de la semana

Noticias y datos recientes, interpretados desde la filosofía de la oficina sostenible y rentable.

La recuperación no rescata a todos los edificios: acelera la selección

Cushman & Wakefield / IREI · 17 julio 2026 / Yardi Matrix–Allwork.Space · 21 julio 2026

Cushman & Wakefield registra la mejor demanda estadounidense en seis años: la absorción móvil de cuatro trimestres alcanzó 14,3 millones de pies cuadrados y mejoraron 49 de 92 mercados.

Pero la vacancia nacional sigue en 20,1% en su muestra. Yardi la sitúa en 17,7%, mientras 11,8 millones de pies cuadrados de oficinas se completaron o estaban en conversión residencial en 2025, máximo histórico.

La recuperación agregada oculta una criba. El activo eficiente, bien ubicado y adaptable recupera liquidez; el edificio sin experiencia, dato operativo o vía de retrofit compite con un uso alternativo.

▸ Lectura Work&Place: El flight to quality ya es economía del activo. Sostenibilidad, coste de ocupación y experiencia presencial forman parte de la defensa de renta, no de una capa reputacional.

▸ Segundo orden / propietario y Real Estate: Si continúa 3-6 meses, el promedio de mercado será menos útil. Crecerá la distancia entre activos con plan de mejora financiable y edificios cuyo mejor business case sea cambiar de uso.

El híbrido se estabiliza: el problema ya no es la presencia, sino su valor

SHRM sobre Bureau of Labor Statistics · 22 julio 2026

El 34,9% de los trabajadores estadounidenses a tiempo completo —32,5 millones— trabajó desde casa al menos parte de una jornada media en 2025. La proporción subió desde 33,4% en 2024.

La intensidad remota baja desde 2021, pero el modelo no desaparece. El acceso varía por función: llega al 56,7% entre titulados de posgrado y cae al 19% entre empleados con educación secundaria.

Para una sede corporativa, imponer el mismo patrón a todos mezcla tareas incompatibles. La pregunta útil es qué trabajo necesita proximidad y qué espacio, horario y calidad ambiental lo hacen mejor.

▸ Lectura Work&Place: La oficina-club y hub de innovación se diseña por momentos de valor: decisión, aprendizaje, creatividad, onboarding y cohesión. La asistencia bruta no mide ninguno.

▸ Segundo orden / CHRO y CFO: Si el híbrido permanece, las empresas pasarán de días obligatorios a portafolios por actividad. Quien mida ocupación sin propósito sobredimensionará espacio o erosionará talento.

El BMS entra en el perímetro de riesgo: un edificio conectado también puede quedar bloqueado

CISA KEV / TechTimes · 19 julio 2026

CISA incluyó CVE-2023-4346 del protocolo KNX en su catálogo de vulnerabilidades explotadas. El fallo puede permitir purgar dispositivos sin opciones de seguridad adicionales y fijar una clave BCU que los bloquee.

KNX gobierna iluminación, climatización, persianas y otros sistemas. El incidente convierte una debilidad digital en riesgo operativo: indisponibilidad, intervención física, pérdida de confort y posible interrupción del inmueble.

La lección no es frenar la conectividad. Es tratar BMS, IoT y automatización como infraestructura crítica, con inventario, segmentación, backups, responsables y plan de recuperación.

▸ Lectura Work&Place: Tecnología con caso de uso operativo incluye coste de fallo. Un edificio inteligente sin gobierno ciberfísico puede ahorrar energía y, a la vez, concentrar riesgo.

▸ Segundo orden / FM, operador y asegurador: Si aumentan los ataques, seguros y contratos exigirán evidencia de parcheo, segmentación y recuperación. El FM necesitará una matriz común con IT y ciberseguridad.

CSRD revela una brecha incómoda: se declara el plan, pero faltan objetivos operativos

EFRAG / ESG Today · 21 julio 2026

EFRAG analizó 905 estados de sostenibilidad FY2025 con aseguramiento. El 69% declara un plan de transición climática, frente al 55% anterior; inmobiliario lidera con 95% y España con 89%.

La ejecución queda por detrás. Cada empresa identifica una media de 6,4 temas materiales, pero fija objetivos solo para 3,3. El 63% liga sostenibilidad a incentivos ejecutivos.

Para inmuebles, el riesgo se desplaza del relato al control: un plan sin línea base por edificio, responsable, presupuesto y dato verificable será difícil de defender ante auditor, banco o consejo.

▸ Lectura Work&Place: La G de ESG baja al activo. BMS, facturas, mantenimiento, ocupación y proveedores deben producir una cadena de evidencia que conecte objetivo, decisión y resultado.

▸ Segundo orden / CFO y propietario: Si la brecha persiste 3-6 meses, crecerá la presión para vincular remuneración y financiación a hitos medibles. El edificio será una unidad de ejecución, no un dato consolidado tardío.

La factura física de la IA aparece fuera de balance, en energía y en agua

Nikkei Asia · 21 julio 2026 / Reuters · 23 julio 2026 / Hegemonía · 21 julio 2026

Nikkei estima 1,65 billones de dólares en compromisos fuera de balance de cinco tecnológicas ligados a centros de datos, alquileres y suministro de GPU: ocho veces más que hace cuatro años.

Reuters informó que un centro de datos australiano asociado a OpenAI abandonó su plan de agua reciclada. La carrera de IA ya compite por capital, red, agua y legitimidad local, no solo por chips.

Para la oficina, comprar IA sin medir su coste total repite el error del edificio lleno de dashboards. Cada caso de uso debe justificar ahorro, disponibilidad, calidad del dato y consumo incremental.

▸ Lectura Work&Place: La IA útil empieza por un problema operativo y termina en una cuenta completa de recursos. La sostenibilidad rentable exige incluir infraestructura, energía, agua y dependencia contractual.

▸ Segundo orden / CEO, CFO y FM: Si la inversión continúa al ritmo actual, subirán las primas por potencia y resiliencia digital. Los proyectos de smart building competirán por presupuesto con la infraestructura corporativa de IA.

03 Indicadores a observar

Datos que separan el análisis riguroso de la opinión.

  • Vacancia de oficinas en EE.UU. 20,1% · Cushman & Wakefield Q2 2026; segunda caída interanual trimestral consecutiva.
  • Demanda móvil de cuatro trimestres +14,3 M ft² · Cushman & Wakefield; séptimo trimestre seguido de mejora y mejor nivel desde 2020.
  • Oficina en conversión residencial 11,8 M ft² · Yardi Matrix; completada o en obra durante 2025, máximo histórico.
  • Trabajo desde casa en una jornada media 34,9% · BLS 2025 vía SHRM; 32,5 millones de trabajadores a tiempo completo.
  • Planes de transición climática declarados 69% · EFRAG, 905 estados CSRD FY2025; inmobiliario alcanza 95% y España 89%.
  • Cobertura de objetivos sobre temas materiales 3,3 de 6,4 · EFRAG; evidencia la distancia entre materialidad declarada y gestión.
  • Vulnerabilidad KNX explotada CVE-2023-4346 · CISA KEV; revisar dispositivos, exposición, claves y mitigaciones del fabricante.
  • Compromisos de infraestructura de IA 1,65 billones USD · Nikkei; obligaciones estimadas fuera de balance, ocho veces más en cuatro años.

04 ¿Qué hoja de ruta me marco?

Una acción concreta para cada perfil. Lectura 8 minutos, salida: una decisión.

PerfilAcción
PropietarioClasificar cada activo como defendible, recuperable o candidato a cambio de uso. Añadir coste de retrofit, renta defendible, vacancia, liquidez y plazo de ejecución.
Inquilino / CHROElegir dos actividades presenciales de alto valor y medir durante 30 días asistencia, resultado, satisfacción, tiempo de viaje y uso real de zonas.
Facility ManagerInventariar KNX, BMS e IoT: versión, exposición, propietario, backup y recuperación. Validar CVE-2023-4346 con IT y proveedor antes del 29 de julio.
Operador / Real EstateCrear un cuadro de mando por edificio con ocupación útil, energía por puesto usado, IAQ, coste operativo, incidencias críticas y CAPEX pendiente.
CFOPedir a cada plan climático tres pruebas: línea base, presupuesto y objetivo por activo. Separar compromisos contractuales de IA del gasto visible.
CEOLlevar a comité una decisión binaria por sede: invertir para hacerla competitiva o preparar reducción/cambio de uso. Evitar el CAPEX cosmético.

en.title: The office recovery becomes an operational filter
keypoints: Improving demand separates defensible assets from offices whose strongest economic case is conversion.
Stable hybrid work makes value by activity more useful than raw attendance.
BMS, CSRD and AI turn data quality and operational resilience into financial variables.
en.body:
01 Executive summary

This week's thesis: the office recovery has become a selection mechanism. Demand is improving, but capital, talent and regulation are drawing a harder line between operable assets and expendable square metres.

Evidence is the common pattern. Useful occupancy, ESG data, cybersecurity and resource consumption now influence rent, CAPEX and productivity. The sustainable office wins when it supports better decisions; space that cannot prove its function, performance and resilience enters discount or conversion territory.

02 Signals of the week

Recent news and data, interpreted through the economics of sustainable and profitable workplaces.

The recovery will not rescue every building: it accelerates selection

Cushman & Wakefield / IREI · 17 July 2026 / Yardi Matrix–Allwork.Space · 21 July 2026

Cushman & Wakefield records the strongest US demand in six years: four-quarter rolling absorption reached 14.3 million square feet, and 49 of 92 markets improved.

Yet national vacancy remains 20.1% in its sample. Yardi puts it at 17.7%, while 11.8 million square feet of office space was completed or under residential conversion in 2025, a record high.

The aggregate recovery hides a filter. Efficient, well-located and adaptable assets regain liquidity; a building without experience quality, operational data or a retrofit route competes against an alternative use.

▸ Work&Place reading: Flight to quality is now asset economics. Sustainability, occupancy cost and the in-person experience help defend rent; they are no longer a reputational overlay.

▸ Second order / owner and Real Estate: If the pattern continues for 3-6 months, market averages will become less useful. The distance will widen between assets with a financeable improvement plan and buildings whose best business case is conversion.

Hybrid work stabilises: presence is no longer the problem, value is

SHRM on Bureau of Labor Statistics data · 22 July 2026

Some 34.9% of US full-time workers — 32.5 million people — worked from home for at least part of an average day in 2025. The share rose from 33.4% in 2024.

Remote intensity has fallen from its 2021 peak, but the model is not disappearing. Access varies by role: it reaches 56.7% among workers with advanced degrees and falls to 19% among those with a high-school education.

For a corporate headquarters, imposing one pattern on everyone mixes incompatible tasks. The useful question is which work needs proximity and which space, schedule and environmental quality make it better.

▸ Work&Place reading: The office as club and innovation hub is designed around moments of value: decisions, learning, creativity, onboarding and cohesion. Raw attendance measures none of them.

▸ Second order / CHRO and CFO: If hybrid work persists, companies will move from mandatory days to activity-based portfolios. Measuring occupancy without purpose will either oversize space or erode talent.

BMS enters the risk perimeter: a connected building can also be locked

CISA KEV / TechTimes · 19 July 2026

CISA added KNX protocol vulnerability CVE-2023-4346 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue. The flaw may allow an attacker to purge devices without additional security options and set a BCU key that locks them.

KNX controls lighting, HVAC, blinds and other systems. The incident turns a digital weakness into operational risk: loss of availability, physical intervention, reduced comfort and possible building disruption.

The lesson is not to stop connectivity. BMS, IoT and automation must be treated as critical infrastructure, with an inventory, segmentation, backups, named owners and a recovery plan.

▸ Work&Place reading: Technology with an operational use case includes the cost of failure. A smart building without cyber-physical governance may save energy while concentrating risk.

▸ Second order / FM, operator and insurer: If attacks increase, insurers and contracts will demand evidence of patching, segmentation and recovery. FM will need a shared control matrix with IT and cybersecurity.

CSRD exposes an awkward gap: plans are declared, but operational targets are missing

EFRAG / ESG Today · 21 July 2026

EFRAG analysed 905 assured FY2025 sustainability statements. Some 69% disclose a climate transition plan, up from 55%; real estate leads at 95% and Spain at 89%.

Execution lags behind. Each company identifies an average of 6.4 material topics but sets targets for only 3.3. Sustainability is linked to executive incentives by 63% of companies.

For property, risk moves from narrative to control: a plan without a building-level baseline, owner, budget and verifiable data will be difficult to defend to an auditor, lender or board.

▸ Work&Place reading: The G in ESG moves down to the asset. BMS, invoices, maintenance, occupancy and suppliers must produce an evidence chain linking target, decision and result.

▸ Second order / CFO and owner: If the gap persists for 3-6 months, pressure will grow to link remuneration and financing to measurable milestones. The building will become an execution unit, not a late consolidated datapoint.

AI's physical bill appears off balance sheet, in energy and in water

Nikkei Asia · 21 July 2026 / Reuters · 23 July 2026 / Hegemony · 21 July 2026

Nikkei estimates $1.65 trillion in off-balance-sheet commitments by five technology companies tied to data centres, leases and GPU supply: eight times the level of four years ago.

Reuters reported that an Australian data centre associated with OpenAI dropped its recycled-water plan. The AI race now competes for capital, grid capacity, water and local legitimacy, not only for chips.

For the office, buying AI without measuring its full cost repeats the mistake of the dashboard-filled building. Every use case must justify savings, availability, data quality and incremental consumption.

▸ Work&Place reading: Useful AI starts with an operational problem and ends with a complete resource account. Profitable sustainability must include infrastructure, energy, water and contractual dependency.

▸ Second order / CEO, CFO and FM: If investment continues at the current pace, premiums for power capacity and digital resilience will rise. Smart-building projects will compete for budget with corporate AI infrastructure.

03 Indicators to watch

Data that separates rigorous analysis from opinion.

  • US office vacancy 20.1% · Cushman & Wakefield Q2 2026; second consecutive quarterly year-on-year decline.
  • Four-quarter rolling demand +14.3M sq ft · Cushman & Wakefield; seventh consecutive quarter of improvement and strongest level since 2020.
  • Office space in residential conversion 11.8M sq ft · Yardi Matrix; completed or under construction during 2025, a record high.
  • Working from home on an average day 34.9% · BLS 2025 via SHRM; 32.5 million full-time workers.
  • Declared climate transition plans 69% · EFRAG, 905 FY2025 CSRD statements; real estate reaches 95% and Spain 89%.
  • Target coverage of material topics 3.3 of 6.4 · EFRAG; evidence of the distance between declared materiality and management.
  • Exploited KNX vulnerability CVE-2023-4346 · CISA KEV; review devices, exposure, keys and vendor mitigations.
  • AI infrastructure commitments $1.65tn · Nikkei; estimated off-balance-sheet obligations, up eightfold in four years.

04 What roadmap should I set?

One concrete action for each profile. Eight-minute read, one decision out.

ProfileAction
OwnerClassify each asset as defensible, recoverable or a candidate for conversion. Add retrofit cost, defensible rent, vacancy, liquidity and execution time.
Tenant / CHROSelect two high-value in-person activities and measure attendance, outcomes, satisfaction, travel time and actual zone use for 30 days.
Facility ManagerInventory KNX, BMS and IoT: version, exposure, owner, backup and recovery. Validate CVE-2023-4346 with IT and the vendor before 29 July.
Operator / Real EstateCreate a dashboard for each building covering useful occupancy, energy per workstation used, IAQ, operating cost, critical incidents and pending CAPEX.
CFORequire three proofs from every climate plan: baseline, budget and target by asset. Separate contractual AI commitments from visible expenditure.
CEOBring a binary decision for each site to the committee: invest to make it competitive or prepare a reduction/conversion. Avoid cosmetic CAPEX.

es.title: La oficina sostenible entra en la fase de rendimiento verificable
keypoints: La oficina sostenible pasa de promesa ESG a prueba de rendimiento operativo.
Sin BMS, sensores, energía y mantenimiento conectados, la IA no genera ROI.
RTO, calor e IAQ obligan a demostrar que la oficina mejora productividad, no solo asistencia.
es.body:
01 Resumen ejecutivo

La tesis de la semana: la oficina sostenible está dejando de ser un programa ESG para convertirse en una infraestructura de decisión. Regulación, energía, IA, calor y retorno a la oficina empujan en la misma dirección: medir mejor, operar antes y justificar cada euro de CAPEX con datos trazables.

El patrón no es más tecnología ni más reporting. Es coordinación: edificios capaces de convertir dato disperso en ahorro, resiliencia, productividad y defensa del valor del activo. Para empresas, activos y personas, la ventaja está en pasar de presencia y promesas a rendimiento verificable.

02 Señales de la semana

Noticias y datos recientes, interpretados desde la filosofía de la oficina sostenible y rentable.

ESRS revisado: menos carga formal, más presión sobre el dato material

Comisión Europea · 3 julio 2026 / Mayer Brown · 13 julio 2026

La Comisión Europea adoptó los ESRS revisados y un estándar voluntario para empresas pequeñas fuera del perímetro CSRD. La revisión reduce más del 60% de los datapoints obligatorios y más del 70% del total.

La señal de esta semana no es que la sostenibilidad pierda peso. Es que el reporting se concentra: menos volumen, más exigencia de materialidad, trazabilidad y evidencia útil para inversores, clientes y financiadores.

Para edificios, esto cambia la conversación. Energía, agua, residuos, climatización, proveedores, ocupación y mantenimiento ya no son anexos técnicos: son fuentes de dato con impacto económico y reputacional.

▸ Lectura Work&Place: La G de ESG baja al FM. El activo competitivo será el que pueda explicar de dónde sale cada dato, quién lo gobierna y qué decisión operativa permite tomar.

▸ Segundo orden / CFO y Real Estate: Si esta simplificación continúa 3-6 meses, el coste se moverá del reporting a la arquitectura del dato. Quien no conecte BMS, facturas, sensores y proveedores tendrá menos burocracia, pero no mejor evidencia.

La IA en edificios entra en la fase incómoda: sin integración no hay ROI

Facility Executive · 13 julio 2026 / Johnson Controls · junio-julio 2026

Facility Executive describió el problema con precisión: los edificios tienen más sensores, dashboards y software, pero muchas operaciones siguen fragmentadas. Un edificio típico opera con 5 a 15 sistemas separados.

Johnson Controls, en su informe 2026 sobre IA y digitalización en FM, sitúa la integración como el cuello de botella. Líderes y FM quieren eficiencia, ciberseguridad y productividad, pero el stack tecnológico crece más rápido que la capacidad de coordinarlo.

La señal económica es directa. La IA no arregla un edificio desconectado: hereda sus silos, multiplica interfaces y deja energía, confort y mantenimiento en modo reactivo.

▸ Lectura Work&Place: Tecnología con caso de uso operativo: no gana el edificio con más herramientas, sino el que conecta dato, control, mantenimiento y experiencia en una cadena de decisión común.

▸ Segundo orden / FM y operador: Si la presión continúa, la prioridad de 2026 no será comprar más IA, sino normalizar datos, protocolos y workflows. El FM pasa de gestor de incidencias a orquestador de rendimiento.

El retorno a la oficina se estabiliza, pero el calor y el talento obligan a rediseñar reglas

Financial News London · 10 julio 2026 / Fortune · 5 julio 2026

Jupiter mantendrá por tercer verano una regla más flexible en agosto, frente a rivales financieros que sostienen políticas presenciales más rígidas. Financial News vincula el movimiento con calor, vacaciones y responsabilidades familiares.

Fortune, con datos de Census y Fed de Minneapolis, mostró que el trabajo remoto e híbrido sigue alrededor del 22% en EE.UU. pese al endurecimiento corporativo del RTO. La presencia vuelve, pero no de forma lineal ni universal.

La oficina deja de competir solo contra casa. Compite contra clima, movilidad, cuidado familiar, coste de desplazamiento y calidad de experiencia presencial.

▸ Lectura Work&Place: La oficina-club y hub de innovación necesita reglas inteligentes. Obligar presencia sin medir valor convierte m2 en coste; diseñar momentos presenciales útiles convierte espacio en productividad social.

▸ Segundo orden / CHRO y CEO: Si el patrón dura 3-6 meses, las políticas RTO tendrán que incorporar estacionalidad, salud térmica y propósito por día. La métrica crítica será valor presencial, no asistencia bruta.

Retrofit deja de ser “proyecto verde” y pasa a ser defensa de valor

RMI / CBRE / ULI · 2025, vigente esta semana por presión regulatoria y de capital

RMI sintetiza el giro: la descarbonización en real estate debe convertirse en aumento de valor, no solo cumplimiento. Cita que cerca del 70% de ocupantes reduciría o rechazaría pagar por edificios sin sostenibilidad operativa.

El mismo informe recoge primas medias de renta del 3%-4% para edificios LEED en EE.UU. y mejor ocupación que activos comparables no certificados. También señala que los activos energéticamente eficientes han superado en retorno a los menos eficientes desde 2021.

Hegemonía refuerza el contexto de la semana: energía, componentes críticos, sanciones y acceso condicionado siguen elevando el coste de operar sin resiliencia.

▸ Lectura Work&Place: La sostenibilidad rentable se decide en CAPEX priorizado: qué activo merece retrofit, qué sistema reduce OPEX, qué mejora ocupación y qué evidencia defiende financiación o valoración.

▸ Segundo orden / propietario y financiador: Si continúa la presión, crecerá el spread entre activos operativamente defendibles y activos obsoletos. El brown discount se parecerá menos a una etiqueta ESG y más a una penalización financiera.

Calidad ambiental interior: el bienestar vuelve como variable de productividad, no como amenity

ISHN · junio 2026 / Harvard Healthy Buildings · evidencia CogFX

ISHN volvió a poner el foco en CO2, humedad, temperatura y contaminantes como variables que afectan errores, output, reuniones y absentismo. La evidencia de Harvard CogFX refuerza que mejor aire interior mejora capacidades cognitivas.

La señal importa esta semana porque RTO, calor y presión de productividad convergen. Si la empresa pide presencia, el espacio debe demostrar que mejora concentración, salud y colaboración frente al trabajo remoto.

La calidad ambiental ya no es una certificación bonita. Es una variable operacional que conecta climatización, energía, salud laboral, absentismo y experiencia de empleado.

▸ Lectura Work&Place: La S de ESG baja al día a día: aire, ruido, iluminación, temperatura y confort deben medirse junto a ocupación y coste, no después en una encuesta anual.

▸ Segundo orden / CHRO y FM: Si la señal continúa, veremos cuadros de mando que mezclen IAQ, quejas térmicas, absentismo, rotación y uso por zona. La salud del edificio será una métrica de talento.

03 Indicadores a observar

Datos que separan el análisis riguroso de la opinión.

  • Datapoints ESRS obligatorios -60%+ · Comisión Europea, ESRS revisados adoptados el 3 de julio de 2026.
  • Datapoints ESRS totales -70%+ · Menos volumen de reporting, más valor del dato material y trazable.
  • Ahorro esperado de costes de reporting >30% por compañía · Objetivo declarado por la Comisión Europea.
  • Sistemas separados por edificio 5-15 · Facility Executive, julio 2026: BMS, sensores, mantenimiento, energía y ocupación suelen operar en silos.
  • Energía desperdiciada por fallos/controles/HVAC 15%-30% · Facility Executive cita investigación de Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory.
  • Caso operativo con sistemas unificados -7% energía · Ejemplo KODE Labs en edificio de 400.000 sq ft, con mejora de confort.
  • Trabajo híbrido/remoto en EE.UU. ~22% · Fortune sobre Census + Fed Minneapolis, enero-febrero 2026.
  • Ocupantes que penalizarían edificios sin sostenibilidad ~70% · RMI/CBRE/ULI: rechazarían o pagarían menos por falta de features y operación sostenible.
  • Prima media de renta LEED 3%-4% · RMI/CBRE/ULI para edificios LEED en EE.UU.
  • Variables IAQ a monitorizar CO2 · PM2.5 · VOC · humedad · temperatura · ISHN/Harvard Healthy Buildings: impacto en rendimiento cognitivo y productividad.

04 ¿Qué hoja de ruta me marco?

Una acción concreta para cada perfil. Lectura 6 minutos, salida: una decisión.

PerfilAcción prioritaria
PropietarioClasificar la cartera en tres grupos: defendible, recuperable con retrofit y vulnerable. Para cada activo, vincular CAPEX, consumo, ocupación, evidencia ESG y riesgo de financiación.
Inquilino / CHRORevisar la política RTO con estacionalidad, propósito por día y métricas de valor presencial: colaboración, mentoring, onboarding, foco, absentismo y rotación.
Facility ManagerHacer un mapa de silos: BMS, HVAC, sensores, mantenimiento, energía, access control y quejas. Elegir una incidencia recurrente y convertirla en workflow integrado.
Real Estate / OperadorPreparar un dashboard mínimo por edificio: ocupación real, energía por m2, quejas térmicas, IAQ, coste por puesto usado y backlog de mantenimiento crítico.
CFOPedir que todo retrofit venga con hipótesis OPEX/CAPEX, impacto en renta u ocupación, riesgo regulatorio evitado y evidencia disponible para financiación o seguro.
CEOLlevar a comité una pregunta simple: qué parte de nuestra oficina mejora productividad y qué parte solo consume coste fijo. Decidir una medición piloto de 30 días.

en.title: The sustainable office enters the age of verifiable performance
keypoints: The sustainable office is moving from ESG promise to operational performance proof.
Without connected BMS, sensors, energy and maintenance, AI will not deliver ROI.
RTO, heat and IAQ force the office to prove productivity, not just attendance.
en.body:
01 Executive Summary

This week’s thesis: the sustainable office is moving from ESG programme to decision infrastructure. Regulation, energy, AI, heat and return-to-office policies are pushing in the same direction: measure better, operate earlier and justify every euro of CAPEX with traceable data.

The pattern is not more technology or more reporting. It is coordination: buildings able to turn scattered data into savings, resilience, productivity and asset-value defence. For companies, assets and people, the advantage is shifting from presence and promises to verifiable performance.

02 Signals of the week

Recent news and data, interpreted through the lens of the sustainable and profitable office.

Revised ESRS: less formal burden, more pressure on material data

European Commission · 3 July 2026 / Mayer Brown · 13 July 2026

The European Commission adopted revised ESRS and a voluntary standard for small companies outside the CSRD perimeter. The revision reduces mandatory datapoints by more than 60% and total datapoints by more than 70%.

This week’s signal is not that sustainability is losing weight. It is that reporting is concentrating: less volume, more demand for materiality, traceability and evidence useful to investors, clients and financiers.

For buildings, this changes the conversation. Energy, water, waste, HVAC, suppliers, occupancy and maintenance are no longer technical appendices: they are data sources with economic and reputational impact.

▸ Work&Place reading: The G in ESG moves down into FM. The competitive asset will be the one able to explain where each datapoint comes from, who governs it and what operational decision it enables.

▸ Second order / CFO and Real Estate: If this simplification continues for 3-6 months, cost will move from reporting to data architecture. Whoever fails to connect BMS, invoices, sensors and suppliers will have less bureaucracy, but not better evidence.

AI in buildings enters the uncomfortable phase: without integration there is no ROI

Facility Executive · 13 July 2026 / Johnson Controls · June-July 2026

Facility Executive described the problem precisely: buildings have more sensors, dashboards and software, but many operations remain fragmented. A typical building operates with 5 to 15 separate systems.

Johnson Controls, in its 2026 report on AI and digitalisation in FM, identifies integration as the bottleneck. Leaders and FM teams want efficiency, cybersecurity and productivity, but the technology stack is growing faster than the ability to coordinate it.

The economic signal is direct. AI does not fix a disconnected building: it inherits its silos, multiplies interfaces and leaves energy, comfort and maintenance in reactive mode.

▸ Work&Place reading: Technology with an operational use case: the winning building is not the one with more tools, but the one that connects data, control, maintenance and experience into a common decision chain.

▸ Second order / FM and operator: If pressure continues, the 2026 priority will not be buying more AI, but normalising data, protocols and workflows. FM moves from incident manager to performance orchestrator.

Return to office stabilises, but heat and talent force rules to be redesigned

Financial News London · 10 July 2026 / Fortune · 5 July 2026

Jupiter will keep a more flexible August rule for a third summer, unlike financial rivals that maintain stricter presence policies. Financial News links the move to heat, holidays and family responsibilities.

Fortune, using Census and Minneapolis Fed data, showed that remote and hybrid work remains around 22% in the US despite the corporate hardening of RTO. Presence is returning, but not linearly or universally.

The office no longer competes only with home. It competes with climate, mobility, family care, commuting cost and the quality of the in-person experience.

▸ Work&Place reading: The office-club and innovation hub needs intelligent rules. Mandatory presence without measured value turns square metres into cost; designing useful in-person moments turns space into social productivity.

▸ Second order / CHRO and CEO: If the pattern lasts 3-6 months, RTO policies will have to incorporate seasonality, thermal health and purpose by day. The critical metric will be in-person value, not gross attendance.

Retrofit stops being a “green project” and becomes value defence

RMI / CBRE / ULI · 2025, still relevant this week because of regulatory and capital pressure

RMI summarises the shift: decarbonisation in real estate must become value creation, not only compliance. It cites that nearly 70% of occupiers would reduce or refuse to pay for buildings without sustainable operational features.

The same report records average rent premiums of 3%-4% for LEED buildings in the US and better occupancy than comparable uncertified assets. It also notes that energy-efficient assets have outperformed less efficient ones in returns since 2021.

Hegemony reinforces this week’s context: energy, critical components, sanctions and conditional access continue to raise the cost of operating without resilience.

▸ Work&Place reading: Profitable sustainability is decided in prioritised CAPEX: which asset deserves retrofit, which system reduces OPEX, what improves occupancy and what evidence defends financing or valuation.

▸ Second order / owner and financier: If pressure continues, the spread will grow between operationally defensible assets and obsolete assets. The brown discount will look less like an ESG label and more like a financial penalty.

Indoor environmental quality: wellbeing returns as a productivity variable, not an amenity

ISHN · June 2026 / Harvard Healthy Buildings · CogFX evidence

ISHN put the spotlight back on CO2, humidity, temperature and pollutants as variables affecting errors, output, meetings and absenteeism. Harvard CogFX evidence reinforces that better indoor air improves cognitive capacity.

The signal matters this week because RTO, heat and productivity pressure are converging. If a company asks people to be present, the space must prove that it improves concentration, health and collaboration versus remote work.

Environmental quality is no longer a nice certification. It is an operational variable connecting HVAC, energy, occupational health, absenteeism and employee experience.

▸ Work&Place reading: The S in ESG moves into the daily operation: air, noise, lighting, temperature and comfort must be measured alongside occupancy and cost, not afterwards in an annual survey.

▸ Second order / CHRO and FM: If the signal continues, we will see dashboards combining IAQ, thermal complaints, absenteeism, turnover and use by zone. Building health will become a talent metric.

03 Indicators to watch

Data that separates rigorous analysis from opinion.

  • Mandatory ESRS datapoints -60%+ · European Commission, revised ESRS adopted on 3 July 2026.
  • Total ESRS datapoints -70%+ · Less reporting volume, more value attached to material and traceable data.
  • Expected reporting cost savings >30% per company · Declared objective of the European Commission.
  • Separate systems per building 5-15 · Facility Executive, July 2026: BMS, sensors, maintenance, energy and occupancy often operate in silos.
  • Energy wasted by faults/controls/HVAC 15%-30% · Facility Executive cites Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory research.
  • Operational case with unified systems -7% energy · KODE Labs example in a 400,000 sq ft building, with improved comfort.
  • Hybrid/remote work in the US ~22% · Fortune on Census + Minneapolis Fed, January-February 2026.
  • Occupiers who would penalise buildings without sustainability ~70% · RMI/CBRE/ULI: would reject or pay less for lack of sustainable features and operations.
  • Average LEED rent premium 3%-4% · RMI/CBRE/ULI for LEED buildings in the US.
  • IAQ variables to monitor CO2 · PM2.5 · VOC · humidity · temperature · ISHN/Harvard Healthy Buildings: impact on cognitive performance and productivity.

04 What roadmap should I set?

One concrete action for each profile. Six-minute read, one decision out.

ProfilePriority action
OwnerClassify the portfolio into three groups: defensible, recoverable through retrofit and vulnerable. For each asset, link CAPEX, consumption, occupancy, ESG evidence and financing risk.
Tenant / CHROReview the RTO policy with seasonality, purpose by day and metrics of in-person value: collaboration, mentoring, onboarding, focus, absenteeism and turnover.
Facility ManagerMap the silos: BMS, HVAC, sensors, maintenance, energy, access control and complaints. Choose one recurring incident and turn it into an integrated workflow.
Real Estate / OperatorPrepare a minimum dashboard per building: real occupancy, energy per m2, thermal complaints, IAQ, cost per used workstation and critical maintenance backlog.
CFORequire every retrofit to come with OPEX/CAPEX assumptions, rent or occupancy impact, avoided regulatory risk and evidence available for financing or insurance.
CEOBring one simple question to the committee: what part of our office improves productivity and what part only consumes fixed cost? Decide on a 30-day measurement pilot.
